ratings.reviewer_notes: Review supports curcumin targeting PI3K/AKT, but the abstract does not explicitly connect this pathway to apoptosis.
Reports curcumin regulation of pro- and antiapoptotic proteins, but no specific mediating genes are identified in the abstract.
Identifies curcumin-regulated pathways and miRNAs, including PI3K/AKT, JAK/STAT, MAPK, p53, and NF-kappaB, but does not explicitly link them to apoptosis in the abstract.
Experimental cell and xenograft study directly links curcumin-induced apoptosis to regulation of Nrf2/NFE2L2 and GPX4 signaling, with pharmacologic reversal evidence.
Links inhibition of PI3K/AKT/mTOR with apoptotic markers, but curcumin was tested in a combination with resveratrol and cisplatin, limiting attribution to curcumin alone.
Focused review explicitly identifies p53, NF-kappaB, COX-2, BCL2, PI3K, and MAPKs as mediators of curcumin-induced apoptosis.

Systematic review identifies NF-kappaB, AKT, androgen receptor, and apoptosis pathways, but emphasizes combined curcumin–ursolic acid evidence and does not establish specific curcumin-to-gene-to-apoptosis links.
Direct experimental evidence shows curcumin altering BCL2, BCL2L1, BIRC5, XIAP, BAX, BAK, BBC3/PUMA, BCL2L11/BIM, PMAIP1/NOXA, DR4, DR5, FADD, CASP3, and CASP9 in association with apoptosis.
Focused review directly links curcumin-mediated STAT3 inhibition to induction of apoptosis in breast cancer.
Systematic review reports modulation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR, NF-kappaB, androgen receptor, and apoptosis regulators, but the abstract aggregates outcomes without a specific mediator-to-apoptosis test.
Review is specifically devoted to pro- and antiapoptotic molecules and signaling pathways involved in curcumin-induced apoptosis, although individual genes are not named in the abstract.
Focused review directly addresses curcumin-induced apoptosis through intrinsic, extrinsic, NF-kappaB, and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways.
Broad review states that curcumin targets signaling pathways and induces apoptosis, but the abstract provides no specific candidate genes or explicit two-hop mechanism.
Review names VEGF, NF-kappaB, mTOR, PI3K/AKT, and EGFR as curcumin targets and separately reports apoptosis, but does not explicitly establish which targets mediate that outcome.
Review addresses curcumin modulation of apoptosis and autophagy in colorectal cancer, but no specific mediating genes are reported in the abstract.
Directly demonstrates curcumin-induced apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells, but NLRP3 is evaluated mainly as a pyroptosis component and is not shown to mediate apoptosis.
Review reports curcumin-induced apoptosis in gastric cancer but does not identify specific gene mediators in the abstract.
Experimental study directly links curcumin nanoparticle treatment to apoptosis through ROS-dependent AMPK, mTOR, and ULK1 autophagy signaling, with antioxidant reversal evidence.
